function: above_phy, p. 1 and p. 7: the learned method decides task offloading (MADDQN) and allocates onboard edge computing resources to tasks (DDPG), both edge computing decisions, not physical-layer functions.
notes: Exclusion reason above_phy (check 4): the learning acts on task offloading and edge computing decisions in a LEO satellite edge computing network. p. 1: "decomposes the JCORA problem into two-layered subproblems, namely global computation offloading and local resource allocation". The offloading action is where to conduct a task, p. 4: "either to conduct the tasks locally, forward them to neighboring satellites via ISLs, or transmit them to the clouds". The resource that DDPG allocates is onboard computation, p. 7: "efficiently allocate the available edge computing resources to the received tasks, thereby minimizing task computation delay"; p. 11: "total compute resource onboard each satellite is set within the range of 2.4 GHz to 4.8 GHz" (CPU capacity, with 14 CPU cycles per bit). The link is not controlled by learning: p. 10: "the allocated network bandwidth for task transmitting on a groundsatellite link and an ISL is set at 15 Mbps and 80 Mbps"; p. 5: "we assign a fixed channel gain hS to SCLs"; transmit power is a fixed parameter in Eqs. (6) and (10). So the satellite-link exception (learned transmit power, resource allocation, or beams) does not apply, and no physical-layer decision is learned jointly. Checks 1 to 3 pass: research article in IEEE TCCN that proposes and evaluates a learned method (MADDQN and DDPG). The PDF is the paper of the DOI: its title and "Digital Object Identifier 10.1109/TCCN.2024.3510562" are on p. 1. Table I (p. 10, read from the PDF image) lists only DRL hyperparameters.
